questions.questionText: The relation between time t and distance x for a moving body is given as t = mx2 + nx, where m and n are constants. The retardation of the motion is : (When v stands for velocity)
questions.questionHtml: The relation between time t and distance x for a moving body is given as t = mx<sup>2</sup> + nx, where m and n are constants. The retardation of the motion is : (When v stands for velocity)
questions.explanationHtml:
The relationship between time $ t $ and distance $ x $ for a moving body is given by $ t = mx^2 + nx $, where $ m $ and $ n $ are constants. To determine the retardation (negative acceleration) of the motion, let's follow the steps to derive it:

Given:

$ t = mx^2 + nx $

First, differentiate $ t $ with respect to $ x $:

$ \frac{dt}{dx} = 2mx + n $

Since velocity $ v $ is defined as $ \frac{dx}{dt} $, we can write:

$ \frac{1}{v} = \frac{dt}{dx} = 2mx + n $

Thus,

$ v = \frac{1}{2mx + n} $

Next, to find the acceleration $ a $ (which is the derivative of velocity with respect to time), we start with the chain rule:

$ \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{dv}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} $

Since $ v = \frac{dx}{dt} $, substituting $ x $ gives:

$ \frac{dx}{dt} = v $

Rewrite it:

$ \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{dv}{dx} \cdot v $

Differentiate $ v $ with respect to $ x $:

$ v = (2mx + n)^{-1} $

$ \frac{dv}{dx} = -\frac{2m}{(2mx + n)^2} $

Then,

$ \frac{dv}{dt} = -\frac{2m}{(2mx + n)^2} \cdot v $

Substitute $ v = \frac{1}{2mx + n} $ into the expression:

$ \frac{dv}{dt} = -\frac{2m}{(2mx + n)^2} \cdot \frac{1}{2mx + n} $

Simplify the expression:

$ \frac{dv}{dt} = -2m \left( \frac{1}{2mx + n} \right)^3 $

$ a = -2m v^3 $

So, the retardation (negative acceleration) is:

$ a = -2m v^3 $

questions.questionText: If $$\left( {\overrightarrow a + 3\overrightarrow b } \right)$$ is perpendicular to $$\left( {7\overrightarrow a - 5\overrightarrow b } \right)$$ and $$\left( {\overrightarrow a - 4\overrightarrow b } \right)$$ is perpendicular to $$\left( {7\overrightarrow a - 2\overrightarrow b } \right)$$, then the angle between $$\overrightarrow a $$ and $$\overrightarrow b $$ (in degrees) is _______________.
questions.questionHtml: If $$\left( {\overrightarrow a  + 3\overrightarrow b } \right)$$ is perpendicular to $$\left( {7\overrightarrow a  - 5\overrightarrow b } \right)$$ and $$\left( {\overrightarrow a  - 4\overrightarrow b } \right)$$ is perpendicular to $$\left( {7\overrightarrow a  - 2\overrightarrow b } \right)$$, then the angle between $$\overrightarrow a $$ and $$\overrightarrow b $$ (in degrees) is _______________.
questions.explanationText:
$$\left( {\overrightarrow a + 3\overrightarrow b } \right) \bot \left( {7\overrightarrow a - 5\overrightarrow b } \right)$$

$$ \therefore $$ $$\left( {\overrightarrow a + 3\overrightarrow b } \right)\,.\,\left( {7\overrightarrow a - 5\overrightarrow b } \right) = 0$$

$$ \Rightarrow $$ $$7{\left| {\overrightarrow a } \right|^2} - 15{\left| {\overrightarrow b } \right|^2} + 16\overrightarrow a \,.\,\overrightarrow b = 0$$ ....(1)

Also, $$\left( {\overrightarrow a - 4\overrightarrow b } \right)\,.\,\left( {7\overrightarrow a - 2\overrightarrow b } \right) = 0$$

$$ \Rightarrow $$ $$7{\left| {\overrightarrow a } \right|^2} + 8{\left| {\overrightarrow b } \right|^2} - 30\overrightarrow a \,.\,\overrightarrow b = 0$$ .....(2)

Equation (1) × 30

$$210{\left| {\overrightarrow a } \right|^2} - 450{\left| {\overrightarrow b } \right|^2} + 480\overrightarrow a \,.\,\overrightarrow b = 0$$ ....(3)

Equation (2) × 16

$$112{\left| {\overrightarrow a } \right|^2} + 128{\left| {\overrightarrow b } \right|^2} - 480\overrightarrow a \,.\,\overrightarrow b = 0$$ .....(4)

from (3) & (4)

$$322{\left| {\overrightarrow a } \right|^2} = 322{\left| {\overrightarrow b } \right|^2}$$

$$ \Rightarrow $$ $${\left| {\overrightarrow a } \right|^2} = {\left| {\overrightarrow b } \right|^2}$$

$$ \Rightarrow $$ $$\left| {\overrightarrow a } \right| = \left| {\overrightarrow b } \right|$$

From equation (2),

$$15\left| {\overrightarrow a } \right| = 30\overrightarrow a .\overrightarrow b $$

$$ \Rightarrow $$ $$15{\left| {\overrightarrow a } \right|^2} = 30\left| {\overrightarrow a } \right|.\left| {\overrightarrow b } \right|\cos \theta $$

$$\cos \theta = {{15} \over {30}} = {1 \over 2}$$

$$\therefore$$ $$\theta = 60^\circ $$

questions.explanationText:
$$y' = {{2y} \over {x\ln x}}$$

$$ \Rightarrow {{dy} \over y} = {{2dx} \over {x\ln x}}$$

$$ \Rightarrow \ln |y| = 2\ln |\ln x| + C$$

put x = 2, y = (ln2)2

$$\Rightarrow$$ c = 0

$$\Rightarrow$$ y = (lnx)2

$$\Rightarrow$$ f(e) = 1

(a + b + c)2 = 1

+ b2

$$ \Rightarrow $$ a2 + b2
+ c2 = – 3 ….(i)

$$ \Rightarrow $$ ab + bc + ca = 2 ….(ii)

Squaring of equation (ii),

$$ \Rightarrow $$ a2b2

$$ \Rightarrow $$ a2b2

$$ \Rightarrow $$ a4 + b4 + c4 – 4 = 9

$$ \Rightarrow $$ a4 + b4 + c4 = 13

questions.questionText: A fair coin is tossed n-times such that the probability of getting at least one head is at least 0.9. Then the minimum value of n is ______________.
questions.questionHtml: A fair coin is tossed n-times such that the probability of getting at least one head is at least 0.9. Then the minimum value of n is ______________.
questions.explanationText:
P(Head) = $${1 \over 2}$$

1 $$-$$ P(All tail) $$\ge$$ 0.9

$$1 - {\left( {{1 \over 2}} \right)^n}$$ $$\ge$$ 0.9

$$ \Rightarrow {\left( {{1 \over 2}} \right)^n} \le {1 \over {10}}$$

$$\Rightarrow$$ nmin = 4
